title: A device in persistent heart failure / Ask whether biventricular pacing is effective

blocks.text: A device in persistent heart failure / Ask whether biventricular pacing is effective

AMaC MRCP PACES · R5-112 · Physical examination · PACES Station 3, cardiovascular · Skills A, B, D, E, G · 10 minutes (up to 6 examination, at least 4 questions) · Guideline dates and links in section 15 · Related AMaC: condition may appear elsewhere in a different context.
An adult with chronic heart failure and an implanted cardiac device remains breathless. Examine the cardiovascular system and discuss the possible purpose and limitations of the device.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text:
HOOK — CRT aims to coordinate ventricular activation in selected HFrEF patients, most strongly supported by broad QRS and LBBB despite guideline-directed treatment.
EXAMINER TRAP — A large device does not tell you CRT-P versus CRT-D, nor does implantation guarantee response.

RELEASED FINDINGS — on inspection, pulse, precordial palpation and auscultation as appropriate: Left infraclavicular device scar, displaced apex, soft S3, mild ankle oedema, no device-site redness, no new murmur.
Question 1 [R4] — What is CRT? | Synchronised pacing to improve function in selected dyssynchronous HFrEF.
Question 2 [R5] — When is benefit strongest? | Symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤35%, LBBB, QRS ≥150 ms despite treatment (ESC 2021).
Question 3 [R6] — CRT-P versus CRT-D? | Pacing alone versus pacing plus defibrillator therapy.
Question 4 [R7] — What if not improving? | Check device capture, rhythm, medications and other causes.
Curveball — If a candidate asks for definitive proof from examination alone: “Explain what examination suggests and which confirmatory tests you need.”

CRT aims to coordinate ventricular activation in selected HFrEF patients, most strongly supported by broad QRS and LBBB despite guideline-directed treatment. A large device does not tell you CRT-P versus CRT-D, nor does implantation guarantee response. Synchronised pacing to improve function in selected dyssynchronous HFrEF. Symptomatic HFrEF, LVEF ≤35%, LBBB, QRS ≥150 ms despite treatment (ESC 2021). Pacing alone versus pacing plus defibrillator therapy.

THINK: Cardiac resynchronisation therapy device.
SAY: CRT aims to coordinate ventricular activation in selected HFrEF patients, most strongly supported by broad QRS and LBBB despite guideline-directed treatment.
DO: Consent, focused cardiovascular examination, present findings and next tests.
NUMBERS: 10-minute examination encounter (PACES23). CRT: LVEF ≤35%, LBBB QRS ≥150 ms (ESC 2021).
TRAP: A large device does not tell you CRT-P versus CRT-D, nor does implantation guarantee response.
FINISH: Explain definitive investigations and appropriate specialist follow-up.
